name: Patel Integrated Logistics Ltd
title: Patel Integrated Logistics Ltd-$ - 526381 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q4 FY26 profit rose on margin and cost control, but the call gave no capacity, utilisation or inventory data; management leaned on promotional claims and a Rajpat subsidiary with no numbers beyond an unsupported 25% revenue add.

triggers.label: International rates up 15% since March
triggers.quote: As I'm talking to you from March, 15%, international rates have increased. So, rates are hardening.

triggers.label: Valuation rerating claim without guidance
triggers.quote: we are expecting very soon the company will have a valuation rerating

guidance.value: adds another 25% to the ~INR400 crore base
guidance.quote: Rajpat will add another 25% from that.
we are expecting a upward of 15% in return on capital employed from that business

red_flags.label: Dividend 30% of PAT on tiny cash base; DSO/ROCE claims unquantified
red_flags.quote: It is basically 30% of our profit after tax

red_flags.label: Non-core property redevelopment, no numbers
red_flags.quote: we are actively pursuing for the redevelopment

evasions.quote: it is very difficult to tell right now
right now immediately we are not looking

summary.headline: FY26 PBT crossed INR10 crore at INR10.30 crore (up ~34%), with PAT of INR9.58 crore and a 30% payout dividend of INR0.40 per share.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 total income from operations up 11.68% YoY to INR96.74 crore, with PBT up nearly 99% to INR3.70 crore and PAT up over 60% to INR2.98 crore. For FY26, total income from operations was INR357.25 crore, PBT INR10.30 crore (up over 34%) and PAT INR9.58 crore (up over 26%). The air freight segment profit rose to INR11.26 crore from INR8.53 crore, and finance cost fell by INR35 lakh to a lower level from INR1.18 crore. A new subsidiary, Rajpat Logistics Limited, was formed in the December 2025 quarter as an additional trucking-booking vertical.

financial_highlights.change: from INR1.18 crore in previous year

segments.name: Air freight logistics
segments.commentary: Segment profit rose to INR11.26 crore in FY26 from INR8.53 crore in FY25. The company says it operates from around 100 airports with more than 60 airlines, and serves pharma, auto parts, engineering, electronics, FMCG and documents.

segments.name: Rajpat Logistics Limited (new subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Formed in the December 2025 quarter; management says it is at a nascent stage. It will book trucking for top corporates on an asset-light basis, and management expects it to add about 25% to the INR400 crore revenue base and to earn ROCE above 15%.

guidance_outlook: Management said momentum continued into April 2026 and expects growth to be maintained.
Rajpat Logistics expected to build meaningful turnover over the next two to three years, with about 25% addition to the current INR400 crore base as per management.
Management expects rates to harden more than volumes; international air rates reportedly up about 15% since March 2026.
No plan to own warehouses or trucks for now; management says current operations earn higher ROCE than warehousing would.
Management expects a valuation re-rating, though no numeric target was given.
capex_capacity: No new capex, capacity or commissioning plans were announced; management said the company is asset-light and will not own trucks.
Management is pursuing redevelopment of a non-core property with two adjacent property owners; a meeting was planned for the following week. No timeline or value was given.
Management said the company is not currently pursuing warehouse assets, though it remains open if returns are attractive.
demand_pricing: Management said industry rates are hardening, with international air rates up about 15% since March 2026, amid supply constraints linked to the geopolitical situation and higher crude and ATF prices.
Management described the environment as favourable for organised players, and expects rate increases to outpace volume growth in FY27.
Passenger aircraft fleet expected to grow from about 700 to about 1,800; government targets airports rising from 140 to 220. Navi Mumbai airport is operational and Jewar is nearing operations.
Management said the company uses an automated system that stops credit when a customer's receivables age beyond a set threshold, to control trade receivables.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue and margin can Rajpat Logistics deliver over three to five years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rajpat would add about 25% to the current INR400 crore revenue base, with ROCE expected above 15%, higher than its margin because capital would turn quickly.

qa_highlights.question: How are the war and higher crude and ATF prices affecting capacity and demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said supply is tight and rates are hardening, with international rates up about 15% since March. Airline-capacity access was described as favourable for organised players with over 60 airlines, and growth momentum was said to continue into April.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company add warehousing capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no plan exists to enter warehousing now, since current operations earn more ROCE than warehousing would, but it remains open if a lucrative opportunity arises.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the mobile app and AI initiatives on revenue leakage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said automation and AI are being used to control leakages, and the receivables system stops credit automatically when outstanding crosses set days. The aim is to raise employee productivity without job losses.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected value and structure of the non-core property redevelopment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is pursuing redevelopment with two adjacent property owners for a larger combined project. It prefers an in-house development structure with recurring income over a one-time sale, and no value was quantified.

risks_watch: Rate-driven growth versus volume: management expects rates to rise faster than volumes, and volume outlook for FY27 was described as difficult to predict.
Fuel and geopolitical exposure: crude and ATF price increases and airline supply constraints tied to the ongoing war were cited.
Rajpat Logistics is at a nascent stage; its revenue and ROCE targets are unproven.
Redevelopment of the non-core property: no value, timeline or structure has been finalised.
Management said the company is 'practically debt free' but still carries a small amount of debt; the exact debt figure was not disclosed.
Dividend of INR0.40 per share is 30% of PAT, which will be watched against FY27 earnings.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on profit growth, dividend and valuation, but vague on specifics such as debt quantum, Rajpat targets and property value. Answers on volume outlook and warehousing were hedged ("never say never"), and some statements were loosely worded.
key_quotes: Profit before tax is INR10.30 crores.
We are a ROCE-driven company, and we are, like I was talking with just now, the subsidiary company, where the ROCE will definitely be more than what we can earn from the warehouse business.
we are very much hopeful that we will be able to maintain the growth in the volume as well.
We will not own any trucks, but we will leverage our network, which we have.

growth.why: Management expects momentum to continue into April 2026 and rate increases to outpace volumes in FY27, with international air rates up about 15% since March 2026; Rajpat Logistics is said to add about 25% to the INR400 crore base over 2-3 years, but no numeric revenue guidance or concrete orders/contracts were given, so backing is vague.
